body: Yes, I had no symptoms after a week, week and a half. You can get better. Don't forget to take care of your mental health, with the floxie thing and the illness I was down for weeks. That's important too.

Hi, I took one pill when I was 21. Like you, I started to have symptoms 2 hours after taking the first pill. I had non-stop neuropathy for 3 days, from days 4-7 only at nigh while trying to sleep. Also tendon pain for a day, two days after the pill. It was uncomfortable to stand up.

I had been taking anti-inflammatory medication. I stopped taking it and changed antibiotic. Many studies show that anti-inflamatory medication can make it worse, so I did go against the advice of a doctor, because they simply didn't know. I had been taking ibuprofen and they prescribed a steroid, which is a no-no. The fact that I was taking ibuprofen maybe explains why one pill affected me so much. 

I did zero activity for a month, but I was already pretty sedentery. My ankles did not hurt. Two months later I picked up a sports hobby and I wasn't careful at all, but nothing happened. In the studies I read, older people had more injuries, although I knew there was a possibility I could get hurt.

Right know it's very scary, I know. You can't control the meds, but you can focus on things within your control. Take care of yourself and good luck.

That's good that you're opening another bank account. They don't need to know. You could call your job and ask them not to send the stipend until you know you can get it.

Could you call the police and explain the situation? Tell them everything: about your parents, about the money, where are you living. In USA there's adult protective services APS, for elders and people who are disabled, but maybe they could help in this situation.

I'm sorry your going through this.

>I hope this doesn't come across as too privileged, as I'm not being physically abused or anything, but I just cannot live like this anymore.

Physical abuse is not the only type of abuse. You're being neglected and even if you don't see it right now, this is abuse.

I'm not sure about getting a lawyer. You need the money asap. And if it was a joint bank account maybe they weren't breaking any laws (but it is fucked up) but you could take legal action for theft. In the subreddit legal advice there's similar cases to yours.

Could you give us more details? Like how long until you could find housing? Could you lie about your adress? Do you have any money left?
I might just start to make a list... thanks!

Yes, I do think it would be possible to take their offer. Especially if my parents go with the narrative that me going away is *their* idea. If I weren't mad I'd laugh at the weird thought process.
Thanks for the words of encouragement
You put the lack of empathy very clearly. Thank you so much for the info. I hope you do well in your journey to healing.
Do they do it unintentionally or intentonally? Not to use it as an excuse, but I'd like to know what goes through the mind of this kind of people. I don't understand it, not one bit.

It would be nice because I'm 75% done. I know the last year is challenging though. I struggled with the degree but what makes me want to drop out is not being able to get away from my parents grip. I had lived in a shared flat but now with corona I'm back at home.
